back: A reduction division: one diploid nucleus divides twice to form four genetically different haploid nuclei.
A maternal and paternal pair with the same genes at the same loci, same size and centromere position; alleles may differ.
Haploid (n): one set of chromosomes (gametes). Diploid (2n): two sets (body cells).

front: What separates in anaphase I and anaphase II?
back: Anaphase I: homologous chromosomes. Anaphase II: sister chromatids (centromeres divide).
A pair of homologous chromosomes together in prophase I and metaphase I: four chromatids.

front: Is there an S phase between meiosis I and II?
back: No: DNA replicates once, before meiosis I.
Metaphase I: bivalents on the equator. Metaphase II: single chromosomes on the equator.

front: Three differences between mitosis and meiosis
back: Mitosis: one division, two identical diploid cells, no pairing. Meiosis: two divisions, four different haploid cells, bivalents and chiasmata.

front: What tissue is squashed to see meiosis in plants?
back: Anthers of young flower buds (pollen mother cells), stained with acetic orcein.
